ideas.title: Build a starter emergency fund before anything else
Pay all non-mortgage debt with the debt snowball, smallest balance first
Pay debts from the highest interest rate down (avalanche)
Build a full emergency fund of three to six months of expenses after the debt is gone
Pause all retirement investing, including the employer match, until consumer debt is gone
Invest fifteen percent of gross income once debt-free with a full emergency fund
Write a zero-based budget before the month begins
Budget from your lowest recent monthly income
Use a realistic income floor and a written priority list for commission months
Build the budget on the predictable paycheck first, then add the variable income
Save in a peak-and-valley or offseason fund for slow months you know are coming
Set up sinking funds for known future expenses
Spread annual and irregular bills into monthly amounts using last year's statements
Protect the Four Walls first: food, utilities, shelter and transportation
Cut nonessentials until the budget balances in a short month
Use cash envelopes for the categories you overspend
Keep a miscellaneous line and send leftovers to the current Baby Step
Keep a small fun money line so the budget lasts
Send every dollar above the plan to the current Baby Step
Sell a financed car you cannot pay off in about two years
Skip debt consolidation and attack the debts directly
Do not cash out retirement accounts to pay debt
Cut up the credit cards and switch to debit and cash
Stop chasing a credit score and build savings instead
Use the emergency fund only for unexpected, necessary and urgent costs
Keep the emergency fund in a plain savings or money market account, not investments
Refill the emergency fund right after using it before resuming other goals
Pause the snowball and stack cash ahead of a baby, job loss or health crisis
Take extra hours or a second job for a season to speed up debt payoff
Sell things you do not need and put the cash toward the current Baby Step
Live on a bare-bones budget for a short season to clear debt faster
Rent until you are debt-free with a full emergency fund before buying a home
If buying a home, use a fifteen-year fixed mortgage with a payment no more than a quarter of take-home pay
Pay cash for cars and never lease
Choose an affordable school and avoid student loans
Get level term life insurance if anyone depends on your income
Keep basic insurance in place at every Baby Step
Hold a monthly budget meeting with your spouse or an accountability partner
Give generously as a planned line in the budget
Save for kids' college only after retirement investing is underway
